title: Normalized site tensor coefficient comparisons
statement: Fix D,C,S and a separated finite-type geometric space X as in [def-sf-mixed-cup-coefficient-data]. There is, for every admissible formal coefficient passage f, a two-variable comparison between scalar extension of the recorded tensor object and the tensor of the two extended inputs. It satisfies all six elementary normalization predicates of [def-sf-mixed-cup-tensor-normalization], [def-sf-mixed-cup-tensor-elementary] and [def-sf-mixed-cup-tensor-closure]. It is natural in both finite-Tor inputs, equals the identity on a formal identity passage, and on a formal composite equals scalar extension of the first comparison followed by the second comparison. No cohomology comparison, compactification, or cup square is asserted.

source.place: Displayed projection/counit composite and final coefficient compatibility sentence; expanded in prop-sf-mixed-cup-coefficient-change proof steps 2--9.

proof.text:
At finite coefficients conjugate the canonical derived scalar balancing
isomorphism by the fixed finite tensor models and the datum's tensor equalities.
At an integral inclusion conjugate the completed tensor scalar comparison by
its recorded normalizations. At reduction take the canonical integral tensor
finite comparison on good flat K-flat representatives. Operation reduction makes
this arrow invertible; its universal representative equation proves the required
formula for every good pair, independently of choices. Rational inclusions are
the localization of the integral comparisons, and localization itself is the
identity on the prescribed tensor object with its equality transports. For
closure represent the inverse common-stage tensor comparison at the input
field, inserting the specified transition unitors. Enlargement of the common
field gives the same morphism class. Each elementary map is natural in both
inputs by its representative construction. The identity passage has the identity
tensor map. Define a formal composite by applying the second scalar functor to
the first tensor map and then the second tensor map. Naturality is preserved by
this operation. Induction on passages gives exactly the displayed identity and
composition equations and all six elementary normalization predicates.

lean.statement: theorem tensorComparisons_exists (S : Operations C) (X : SixFunctorSpace D) [IsSeparated X.obj.hom] : ∃ tensorIso : ∀ {a b : Stage C} (f : Passage C a b), TensorComparison C S X f, (FiniteTensorNormalized C S X tensorIso) ∧ (IntegralTensorNormalized C S X tensorIso) ∧ (RationalTensorNormalized C S X tensorIso) ∧ (ReductionTensorNormalized C S X tensorIso) ∧ (LocalizationTensorNormalized C S X tensorIso) ∧ (ClosureTensorNormalized C S X tensorIso) ∧ (∀ {a b : Stage C} (f : Passage C a b) {K K' L L' : (domain C X.obj.left a).FullSubcategory} (k : K ⟶ K') (l : L ⟶ L'), (change C X f).map (tensorMap C S X a k l) ≫ (tensorIso f K' L').hom = (tensorIso f K L).hom ≫ tensorMap C S X b ((change C X f).map k) ((change C X f).map l)) ∧ (∀ (a : Stage C) (K L : (domain C X.obj.left a).FullSubcategory), (tensorIso (.identity a) K L).hom = 𝟙 _) ∧ (∀ {a b d : Stage C} (f : Passage C a b) (g : Passage C b d) (K L : (domain C X.obj.left a).FullSubcategory), (tensorIso (.comp f g) K L).hom = (change C X g).map ((tensorIso f K L).hom) ≫ (tensorIso g ((change C X f).obj K) ((change C X f).obj L)).hom)
